sentences[0].whyEn: The subordinate variant: Nachdem + past perfect.
sentences[1].whyEn: The main-clause variant: Danach/Anschließend in position 1.
sentences[10].whyEn: The conjunction-less condition: verb first — Regnet es, …
sentences[14].whyEn: Dazu/Zu diesem Zweck — the purpose as an adverb.
help.tips[0].examples[1].en: Before the meeting began, the documents were handed out (×3).
help.tips[0].check.whyEn: After a semicolon you need the main-clause adverb, and the verb comes right after it. nachdem would send the verb to the end, and nach needs a noun.
help.tips[0].en.text: Nebensatz: nachdem, bevor, während, seit(dem), bis, sobald, als, wenn. Hauptsatz: danach, davor / zuvor, währenddessen, seitdem, inzwischen, dann. Nominal: nach, vor, während, seit, bis (zu), bei + noun.
help.tips[0].en.title: Temporal: three columns
help.tips[1].examples[0].en: Because of the rain we stayed (×3).
help.tips[1].examples[1].en: The road is closed, for the bridge is being renovated.
help.tips[1].check.whyEn: folglich is a main-clause adverb, so the verb follows it (kamen wir). weil would put the verb last, and wegen needs a noun in the genitive.
help.tips[1].en.text: Nebensatz: weil, da, zumal. Hauptsatz: deshalb, deswegen, daher, folglich, somit, nämlich (after the verb), denn (coordinating). Nominal: wegen, aufgrund, infolge, dank, aus, vor + noun.
help.tips[1].en.title: Causal: three columns
help.tips[2].examples[0].en: I'll explain it again so that everyone understands. For this purpose I use an example.
help.tips[2].examples[1].en: To prepare for the exam I read the newspaper daily (×2).
help.tips[2].check.whyEn: The two clauses have different subjects (wir / niemand), so you need damit with a full clause. um … zu only works when the subject is the same.
help.tips[2].en.text: Nebensatz: damit (different subjects), um … zu (same subject). Hauptsatz: dazu, zu diesem Zweck, dafür. Nominal: zu, zwecks (+Gen), für + noun. Zur Verbesserung der Qualität = um die Qualität zu verbessern.
help.tips[2].en.title: Final: damit / um … zu / zu + noun
help.tips[3].examples[0].en: Should it rain, we stay. — Otherwise we go. — In case of rain we stay.
help.tips[3].check.whyEn: With no conjunction, the verb moves to position one to make the condition: Brauchen Sie Hilfe, … Falls would need the verb at the end, and bei takes a noun.
help.tips[3].en.text: Nebensatz: wenn, falls, sofern, im Fall, dass. Hauptsatz: verb in position 1 (Regnet es, bleiben wir), or dann / sonst / andernfalls (Es regnet? Dann bleiben wir. Nimm einen Schirm, sonst wirst du nass). Nominal: bei, im Falle (+Gen), ohne, mit + noun.
help.tips[3].en.title: Conditional: wenn / verb-first / bei
help.tips[3].en.trap: the verb-first conditional (Regnet es, …; Sollte es regnen, …) looks like a question. It isn't: the comma and the main clause that follows make it a condition.
help.context.en: After the data had been collected, the evaluation began; meanwhile the publication was already being prepared. As the results were clear-cut, a second survey was dispensed with – to save time. So that the findings remain comparable, the same questions were asked; should a deviation nevertheless appear, it is to be documented. In case of uncertainties the project management is to be informed, otherwise the conclusion is delayed.
help.mistakes[2].whyEn: The verb-first conditional takes a comma, not a question mark.
help.vocab[3].en: so that, in order to / to that end / for that purpose
help.hookEn: Say when, why, what for and under which condition in three ways — clause, adverb or noun — and pick the one that flows.
help.introEn: Adverbial clauses form a system: nine relations, and for each one three ways to express it — a subordinate clause (verb last), a main-clause version with an adverb (verb second) or a special word order, and a nominal version with a preposition. This quiz covers the first four relations. Temporal: nachdem / bevor / während / seit / bis / sobald ↔ danach / davor / währenddessen / seitdem / inzwischen ↔ nach / vor / während / seit / bis + noun. Causal: weil / da ↔ deshalb / daher / folglich / denn ↔ wegen / aufgrund / infolge / dank + noun. Final: damit / um … zu ↔ dazu / zu diesem Zweck ↔ zu / zwecks / für + noun. Conditional: wenn / falls / sofern ↔ verb-first clause (Regnet es, bleiben wir) or dann / sonst / andernfalls ↔ bei / im Falle / ohne + noun. Fluency means having all three variants available for each and choosing by rhythm and register — three subordinate clauses in a row are as heavy as three nominal phrases, and alternation is what makes prose readable. Formal texts draw on all three columns.
help.rememberEn[0]: Each relation × three forms: Nebensatz (verb last) · Hauptsatz (adverb, verb second) · nominal (preposition + noun).
help.rememberEn[1]: temporal nachdem/danach/nach · kausal weil/deshalb/wegen · final damit/dazu/zu · konditional wenn/verb-first/bei.
